title: protocol-agnostic-ingress-shim-design-notebook
content:
Purpose:
- Capture a lightweight, prototype-first design for a protocol-agnostic ingress shim that sits between customer-facing frontends (HTTP/gRPC/websocket/edge-proxy) and Redwood routing/runtime.
- Goal: present a single, small footprint adapter that normalizes request envelopes, performs minimal auth/telemetry, and forwards to internal routing with negotiated capabilities.

Design goals / constraints:
- Protocol-agnostic: support HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, gRPC, websocket, and a light custom binary/frame transport used by some edge clients.
- Small surface: keep the public API tiny (1-2 endpoints) and express capabilities via headers/metadata.
- Zero-trust friendly: no session state kept unless explicitly requested (stateless per-request), but support optional local ephemeral caches (prefetch hints, KV warm).
- Pluggable transforms: allow inserting lightweight transforms (sanitizer, header-mapper, prompt-normalizer).
- Backwards compatible: can be deployed in front of existing frontends without changes to customers (feature-flagged).
- Telemetry: high-cardinality sampling at ingress time, with ability to attach correlation ids to internal RPCs.

High-level flow (text diagram):

[Client]--(HTTP/gRPC/WS)-->[Edge Proxy / CDN]--(orig proto)-->[Ingress Shim]--(Internal gRPC)-->[Routing API]-->[Runtime]
                                 |
                                 +--> optional local transform plugins (lua/wasm)

Ingress responsibilities (minimum viable):
- Normalize incoming request into IngressEnvelope (see API sketch).
- Validate client auth token (delegated to auth service or local short-lived cache).
- Attach x-redwood-ingress-id + timestamp and forward.
- Optionally: extract hints (prompt prefix, expected seq len, prefer-quant, latency-slo) and add to envelope.
- Fast-path passthrough for streaming workloads (do not buffer large token streams).

IngressEnvelope (proto-like sketch):
- envelope_id: string (uuid)
- client_id: string (if present)
- request_type: {TEXT_GENERATION | CHAT | EMBEDDING | RERANK}
- transport_meta: map<string,string> (original proto info: http_method, path, grpc_method, ws_channel)
- capability_hints: list<string> (e.g., low_latency, batching_ok, allow_partial_stream)
- payload: bytes (opaque; for text types this is UTF-8 prompt bundle)
- streaming: boolean
- prewarm_keys: list<string> (optional keys for KV warm/cache)
- provenance: {origin_ip: string, cf_ray: string, user_agent: string}  <-- keep flat in actual JSON header mapping

Implementation notes (practical):
- Keep the envelope small. Use binary gRPC protobuf on the wire internally. But shim should accept multiple external encodings and translate.
- For websocket: support two modes: 1) passthrough frames forwarded as streaming tokens; 2) multiplexed control frames (start/stop/ack).
- Use a small plugin host for transforms: WASM recommended (isolate safety, language neutral). Start by supporting a 3-function contract: on_ingress(envelope) -> envelope | reject; on_stream_chunk(chunk) -> chunk | drop; on_response(resp) -> resp

Config shape (yaml-like example to put in route manifest / infra):
ingress_shim:
  enabled: true
  listen: 0.0.0.0:8081
  tls: auto
  auth_cache_ttl_s: 15
  plugins:
    - name: prompt-normalizer
      kind: wasm
      config: {trim_long_prefix: true}
    - name: allowlist-blocker
      kind: lua
      config: {blocklist_set: s3://redwood-configs/blocklists/default.txt}
  capability_map:
    "/v1/generate": [low_latency, streaming_ok]
    "/v1/embeddings": [batching_ok]

Routing contract (internal gRPC method stub):
rpc Ingress.Dispatch(IngressEnvelope) returns (DispatchAck)
- DispatchAck contains: routing_key, routed_to_cluster, estimated_queue_ms
- Ingress.Shim should respect routing hints but ultimately defer to routing service decisions.

Compatibility negotiation (core idea):
- Client->Shim: supported_features header (comma list). Shim attaches intersection with runtime-feature-set header.
- If no overlap for required features, shim returns 406 with suggested capability alternatives.

Edge cases and decisions:
1) Long lived connections: keep-shim stateless, but maintain a lightweight connection table (conn_id -> last_seen) only to correlate stream fragments for telemetry. Persist minimal tombstones for reconnect.
2) Large request payloads (> 1MB): reject at shim or stream directly to object store and pass reference in envelope.
3) Multi-tenant isolation: shim must emit tenant headers; avoid doing encryption or heavy crypto operations — delegate to downstream private key exchange for enterprise/private deployments.

Performance considerations / SLOs:
- Target p99 additional latency introduced by shim <= 2ms for the fast-path (local cache hit, no plugins).
- Plugin execution time budget: 1ms per plugin for on_ingress path; enforce resource isolation for wasm modules.
- Memory: shim should be small (< 200MB resident) in typical config.

Compatibility table (quick):
- HTTP/1.1: full support (non-streaming and chunked streaming).
- HTTP/2: full support (multiplexed streams).
- gRPC: full support via native gRPC server or gRPC-web translation.
- WebSocket: support streaming, control frames; rehydration heuristics for reconnect.
- Custom binary: must provide a codec plugin that maps frames -> envelope.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we move auth verification entirely to the shim or a shared auth middleware? (tradeoff: latency vs centralization).
- Strategy for schema evolution of IngressEnvelope (versioning header vs content negotiation).
- Should we add a small local prefix/KV cache to warm runtime KV/caches? If so, eviction policy (LRU vs TTL) and soft limits.
- Prototype plan: build a minimal shim in Go that accepts HTTP/gRPC, maps to internal proto, and supports a single wasm plugin host. Measure cold-start latency, p99.

Experiment matrix (MVP 3-step):
1) PoC: go binary, no plugins, accept HTTP/gRPC, translate to proto, forward to routing service. Measure overhead. (owner: Avery)
2) Add wasm host and 1 plugin (prompt-normalizer). Run canary on internal test frontends. (owner: Maya)
3) Full feature flag roll to limited customer cohort with telemetry + auth cache enabled. (owner: Liam)

Notes to self: keep the first prototype intentionally small. Avoid pushing too many config knobs up front. If this lands well, we can later factor out more advanced features into Redwood Optimize suggestions (e.g., capability mapping per-route).

Quick references:
- related tickets: JIRA-RT-4321 (ingress shim MVP), JIRA-SEC-215 (auth cache threat model)
- deps: wasm runtime crate, redwood-internal/grpc-routing v2.1

End.
